cards.text: About eight days after Jesus tells His disciples He must suffer, be killed and be raised to life (Luke 9:22), He takes three of them with Him: Peter, John and James. Out of the whole group, only THREE get the invite. Friend, the last time I got picked out of a group, I was in a clearance bin with a 25 cent sticker on my face.

cards.question: Jesus takes Peter, John and James up on a mountain. What does He go up there to do?

cards.text: So up on the mountain, Jesus prays. And as He's praying, the appearance of His face changes.

cards.question: As Jesus prays on the mountain, His clothes become radiantly ___.

cards.text: Then, SUDDENLY, two men are there talking with Jesus: Moses, who led Israel long ago, and Elijah, the prophet. Friend, if two people showed up in my bakery out of nowhere, I'd be face first in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Moses and Elijah are talking with Jesus on the mountain. What do they talk about?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Peter and his companions are overcome by sleep, with Moses and Elijah RIGHT THERE. Friend, I can't judge, because I lay in a junk drawer for YEARS without doing a single thing.

cards.question: True or false: by the time Peter and his companions wake up, Moses and Elijah are already gone.
When Peter and his companions wake up, they see Jesus' ___ and the two men standing with Him.

cards.text: As Moses and Elijah are leaving, Peter speaks up: “Master, it is good for us to be here.” And Peter's got an idea, friend.

cards.question: Peter wants to put up three ___ on the mountain: one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah.
Right after Peter's idea about the shelters, Luke adds a short note about Peter. What does it say?

answers.text: He did not know what he was saying
He was speaking for all three of them
He had been planning it for days

cards.text: Peter isn't even done talking when a cloud appears and wraps all around them. I know that feeling, friend: the oven timer goes off every time I start a good story.

cards.question: True or false: the disciples are afraid as they enter the cloud.

cards.text: Then a voice comes from the cloud. Everybody gets quiet now, friend. Even me.

cards.question: The voice from the cloud says Jesus is His ___, whom He has chosen.
True or false: the voice from the cloud tells the disciples to listen to Moses and Elijah.

cards.text: After the voice has spoken, the disciples look around the mountain.

cards.question: After the voice from the cloud has spoken, who is still there with the disciples?
True or false: in those days, the disciples tell everyone what they saw on the mountain.

findings.problem: No earlier card gives the baker a way to reason out the color of Jesus' clothes. Card 3 says only that His face changes, so white, golden and purple are equally likely, and a right pick comes down to luck. It is the same kind of detail-guessing that the Psalm 23 oil example marks as bad. Because several other choice cards in this stop are also discovery questions, this one should be reworked. Either give setup the baker can reason from, or ask about something they can work out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Card 10 sets up only that Peter has an idea. It gives nothing that would help the baker choose shelters over altars or towers. Altars are an especially believable thing for Peter to suggest, so a right pick is luck. This is guessing a detail, not reasoning one out.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then a voice comes from the cloud.' 'Everybody gets quiet now, friend.' 'Even me.' Only the opening card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Everybody gets quiet now' is told in the present tense of the scene, so it reads as a fact about the people on the mountain. The text never says anyone went quiet, and Peter was speaking when the cloud came (Luke 9:34). As a storyteller's line, it adds a fact.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.
